**Synopsis:**
A Reuters newsletter arguing that the U.S.-Iran war has functioned as a de facto demand-destruction mechanism for oil globally, accelerating the energy transition. China's Q2 2026 CO₂ emissions fell 1% YoY driven by a 9% oil demand drop and faster-than-expected EV adoption. Globally, renewables are on track to become the top electricity source in 2026 per IEA. The IEA projects gas-fired generation to rise 1.5% in 2027 even as coal dips. The U.S. is structurally insulated from the supply shock as a net oil exporter, giving the Trump administration strategic patience in the conflict. Secondary themes cover European grain stress, climate-linked flood risks, robusta coffee climate resilience doubts, and a near-100%-probability record El Niño through early 2027.
